editorial:
Imagine a guy who used to be a huge deal in action movies and prize fighting, but now he is just a washed-up mess. That is exactly who you get with Sensai Houston. He is desperate to win back his ex-wife, so he decides to blackmail a B-list Hollywood producer to get his own martial arts talk show funded. It is shot like a mockumentary, which means it feels like a fake reality show. The vibe is super goofy and lighthearted, making you feel like you are watching a train wreck that you just cannot look away from. It does not take itself seriously at all, which is where all the fun comes from.

You will love how the movie pokes fun at the ego of old action stars. The acting feels natural for the style, and the comedy hits most of the time. While some parts of the story drag a bit, the sheer weirdness of the setup keeps you interested. If you enjoy awkward humor and martial arts tropes, you should definitely give this a try.
endingExplained: In the final act, the talk show becomes a total disaster, but it actually brings Sensai Houston some unexpected fame. He realizes that his ego was the real problem all along. After a chaotic final confrontation, he manages to make peace with his past. While he does not get everything he wanted right away, he finds a new sense of purpose. The movie wraps up with him finally accepting who he is today rather than clinging to his old glory.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves martial arts movies and awkward comedies.
